"'''Tha Crossroads'''" is a song written and performed by American [[hip hop music|hip hop]] group [[Bone Thugs-n-Harmony]], released as a single in April 1996 by [[Ruthless Records]]. The song is dedicated to the group's mentor, the late [[gangsta rap]]per [[Eazy-E]], and other family members. The song was the highest-debuting rap single when it debuted at number two on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], reaching number one the following week and staying there for eight consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1996-06-15-ca-15136-story.html|title=Seeking a Path After 'Tha Crossroads'|last=Cuda|first=Heidi Siegmund|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=June 15, 1996|access-date=October 20, 2015|issn=0458-3035}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Simmon |first=Sheila |date=May 16, 1996 |title=Crossroad #1 Pop Song |url=https://cleveland.newsbank.com/sign-up?docref=doc/image/v2%253A122AFBBA107AC9E4%2540NGPA-OHPD-17A67BBFDD1B3341%25402450220-17A33D251ED6C480%254061-17A33D251ED6C480%2540%3Fsearch_terms%3Dtha%252Bcrossroads%252Bbone%252Bthugs%252Bn%252Bharmony%26text%3Dtha%2520crossroads%2520bone%2520thugs%2520n%2520harmony%26content_added%3D%26date_from%3D%26date_to%3D%26pub%25255B0%25255D%3D122AFBBA107AC9E4%26sort%3Dold%26pdate%3D1996-05-16 |work=Cleveland Plain Dealer}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Bronson |first=Fred |url=http://archive.org/details/billboardbookofn0000bron_f8a3 |title=The Billboard book of number 1 hits |date=2003 |publisher=Billboard Books |location=New York |via=Internet Archive |isbn=978-0-8230-7677-2 |page=846 |quote=The following week it went to number one, the quickest move to the top since the Beatles took only two weeks to achieve pole position in 1964.}}</ref> It also reached number one in New Zealand, where it was the most successful single of 1996. In 1997, the song won a [[Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group|Grammy for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group]].<ref name="allmusic.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/bone-thugs-n-harmony-mn0000081316/biography|title=Bone Thugs-N-Harmony {{!}} Biography & History {{!}} AllMusic|website=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=October 20, 2015}}</ref>

"Tha Crossroads" is a song written and performed by American hip hop group Bone Thugs-n-Harmony, released as a single in April 1996 by Ruthless Records. The song is dedicated to the group's mentor, the late gangsta rapper Eazy-E, and other family members. The song was the highest-debuting rap single when it debuted at number two on the US Billboard Hot 100, reaching number one the following week and staying there for eight consecutive weeks. It also reached number one in New Zealand, where it was the most successful single of 1996. In 1997, the song won a Grammy for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
"Crossroad" originally debuted in 1995 on the ''[[E. 1999 Eternal]]'' album. It was dedicated to Bone's late friend Wallace (Wally) Laird III, but after the death of Eazy-E they decided to remake it as "Tha Crossroads". The original song appears on the edited version of the album, though the European release has the original as track number 8 and the remix as track 18. The song is performed by four of the group's members, ([[Krayzie Bone]], [[Layzie Bone]], [[Bizzy Bone]] and [[Bone Thugs-n-Harmony|Wish Bone]]). After receiving high praise for their song the group decided to make it their third single for their already released album, ''[[E. 1999 Eternal]]''.

In 2019, a version including group member [[Flesh-n-Bone]] was released with the Bone Thugs-n-Harmony compilation album Lost Archives Vol 1, after receiving their publishing rights from Ruthless Records.

"Crossroad" originally debuted in 1995 on the E. 1999 Eternal album. It was dedicated to Bone's late friend Wallace (Wally) Laird III, but after the death of Eazy-E they decided to remake it as "Tha Crossroads". The original song appears on the edited version of the album, though the European release has the original as track number 8 and the remix as track 18. The song is performed by four of the group's members, (Krayzie Bone, Layzie Bone, Bizzy Bone and Wish Bone). After receiving high praise for their song the group decided to make it their third single for their already released album, E. 1999 Eternal.

In 2019, a version including group member Flesh-n-Bone was released with the Bone Thugs-n-Harmony compilation album Lost Archives Vol 1, after receiving their publishing rights from Ruthless Records.

sections.heading: Reception
sections.wikitext:
The song was a hit worldwide and reached the top of the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and the [[Recorded Music NZ|New Zealand Singles Chart]].<ref name="hot100"/><ref name="nz"/> It was the highest-debuting rap single ever when it entered the national singles chart at #2<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cuda |first=Heidi Siegmund |date=June 15, 1996 |title=Seeking a Path After 'Tha Crossroads' |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1996-06-15-ca-15136-story.html |access-date=July 15, 2025 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> and a week later became #1<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Bone Thugs-N-Harmony {{!}} Biography, Music & News |url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/bone-thugs-n-harmony/ |access-date=July 15, 2025 |magazine=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref> making it the fastest single to rise to the top position on the charts since the [[The Beatles|Beatles]] with "[[Can't Buy Me Love]]" in 1964.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Willow |first=Molly |title=From the Archives: Bizzy Bone's Complicated Feelings about Columbus |url=https://www.columbusmonthly.com/story/lifestyle/2019/07/08/from-archives-bizzy-bone-s/4603395007/ |access-date=July 15, 2025 |website=Columbus Monthly |language=en-US}}</ref>  The song earned them a Grammy award in 1997 for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bone Thugs-N-Harmony {{!}} Artist {{!}} GRAMMY.com |url=https://grammy.com/artists/bone-thugs-n-harmony/8123 |access-date=July 15, 2025 |website=grammy.com}}</ref>

On the New Zealand chart, it was the most successful song of 1996.<ref name="nzye" /> It has been certified double platinum in the United States and platinum in New Zealand.<ref name="uscert" /><ref name="nzcert" /> In 2008, "Tha Crossroads" was ranked number 33 on [[VH1]]'s "100 Greatest Songs of Hip Hop".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stereogum.com/24391/vh1s_100_greatest_hiphop_songs-2/franchises/list/|title=VH1's 100 Greatest Hip-Hop Songs|last=Singh|first=Amrit|website=[[Stereogum]]|date=September 29, 2008|access-date=December 24, 2021}}</ref>
sections.text:
The song was a hit worldwide and reached the top of the US Billboard Hot 100 and the New Zealand Singles Chart. It was the highest-debuting rap single ever when it entered the national singles chart at #2 and a week later became #1 making it the fastest single to rise to the top position on the charts since the Beatles with "Can't Buy Me Love" in 1964.  The song earned them a Grammy award in 1997 for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group.

On the New Zealand chart, it was the most successful song of 1996. It has been certified double platinum in the United States and platinum in New Zealand. In 2008, "Tha Crossroads" was ranked number 33 on VH1's "100 Greatest Songs of Hip Hop".

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The music video was filmed on February 27–28, 1996. It opens with the female vocal group Tre' (Kimberly Cromartie, Rebecca Forsha and Maniko Williams) singing the traditional spiritual "[[Mary Don't You Weep]]" in a church funeral setting, followed by the members of Bone Thugs-n-Harmony singing the main song in several settings, such as a church and a mountain top.

The main focus of the video is a big, imposing man wearing sunglasses, a black hat, and a trench coat, akin to a [[death (personification)|Reaper]]. Bone are among the few who can see the man, and watch him as he gathers souls of various individuals who are marked for death, such as a young man who leaves his distraught mother behind (presumably having died after entering life as a gang member), Bone's friend Wally, Wish Bone's Uncle Charles, Eazy-E, and a newborn baby (possibly having died from a childbirth complication). The Reaper leads the souls, with the baby in his arms, up a mountain where he reveals himself to be an angel, then takes the dead to [[Heaven]].

At the 1996 MTV Video Music Awards, the song was nominated for Video of the Year, Best Group Video, [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Rap Video|Best Rap Video]] (it lost to Coolio's [[Gangsta's Paradise]]), Viewer's Choice and Best Special Effects.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bone Thugs-N-Harmony - Awards |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2060114/awards/ |access-date=July 15, 2025 |website=IMDb |language=en-US}}</ref> The group performed the song live at the ceremony.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fitzgerald |first=Sidney MaddenSidney MaddenContributing Authors: Trent |date=September 4, 2023 |title=Bone Thugs-N-Harmony Perform 'Tha Crossroads' at 1996 MTV Video Music Awards - Today in Hip-Hop |url=https://www.xxlmag.com/today-hip-hop-bone-thugs-n-harmony-perform-tha-crossroads-1996-mtv-vmas/ |access-date=July 15, 2025 |website=XXL Mag |language=en}}</ref>

Bone are among the few who can see the man, and watch him as he gathers souls of various individuals who are marked for death, such as a young man who leaves his distraught mother behind (presumably having died after entering life as a gang member), Bone's friend Wally, Wish Bone's Uncle Charles, Eazy-E, and a newborn baby (possibly having died from a childbirth complication). "Crossroads", a retitled and reworked version of "Tha Crossroads", was released by British ten-piece hip-hop group Blazin' Squad as their first single in August 2002. It topped the UK Singles Chart on the week of August 25, 2002.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: The group's cover version of "Crossroads" was recorded for inclusion on their first studio album, ''[[In the Beginning (Blazin' Squad album)|In the Beginning]]''. The decision to record and release "Crossroads" came about during the final stages of the album production: until June 2002, the song "Standard Flow" was planned for release as the group's first single, with a promotional version of the "Standard Flow" even made available on August 5. Despite being labelled as a cover version, only the chorus from the original version remains, with the verses replaced by new lyrics written by the band. Despite being the only 'cover version' the group ever recorded, it became the band's only number one single, staying at the top of the [[UK Singles Chart]] for one week in August 2002.<ref name="British Hit Singles & Albums">{{cite book | first= David | last= Roberts | year= 2006 | title= [[British Hit Singles & Albums]] | edition= 19th | publisher= Guinness World Records Limited  | location= London | isbn= 1-904994-10-5 | page= 676}}</ref> Two versions of the song exist: the main version, which features in the music video and on ''In the Beginning'', and the full version, which contains two extra verses, which appears on the second physical release of the single.
sections.text: The group's cover version of "Crossroads" was recorded for inclusion on their first studio album, In the Beginning. The decision to record and release "Crossroads" came about during the final stages of the album production: until June 2002, the song "Standard Flow" was planned for release as the group's first single, with a promotional version of the "Standard Flow" even made available on August 5. Despite being labelled as a cover version, only the chorus from the original version remains, with the verses replaced by new lyrics written by the band. Despite being the only 'cover version' the group ever recorded, it became the band's only number one single, staying at the top of the UK Singles Chart for one week in August 2002. Two versions of the song exist: the main version, which features in the music video and on In the Beginning, and the full version, which contains two extra verses, which appears on the second physical release of the single.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The music video for "Crossroads" directed by [[Vaughan Arnell]] was premiered in July 2002. The video runs for a total length of three minutes and forty-eight seconds<ref>{{YouTube|MXh3sueSxps}}</ref> and shows the band performing the song on top of an unfinished flyover in the centre of Cape Town. The video also shows scenes of an underpass where a number of homeless people are living, and individual shots of each band member. The video was filmed with the phantom effect, which provides a 'shadow' type movement for each member of the band.
